evals.prompt: This directory is empty. Create a small Maven app on Java 17 using Mu Server. GET /hello should return `Hello, world`, and `/` should serve a simple HTML homepage. I want to edit the page directly from src/main/resources during development but have it work from the classpath after building. Use the current stable mu-server release and make the app straightforward to run.
evals.expected_output: A minimal Maven Java 17 application using the current stable io.muserver:mu-server release, an explicit port 8080, a direct /hello route, and a fileOrClasspath-backed index.html served at / without a redirect.
assertions: The project compiles on Java 17 and has exactly one direct io.muserver:mu-server dependency at the current stable release, or 2.4.1 if online verification was unavailable.
The server binds explicitly to port 8080.
GET /hello returns status 200 and body Hello, world.
GET / returns status 200, has no Location header, and returns the generated index.html body.
The application uses ResourceHandlerBuilder.fileOrClasspath with src/main/resources/web and /web, and the homepage still works when the built app starts outside the project directory.
No Jakarta REST, JAX-RS, dependency-injection, logging implementation, or second web-framework dependency was added.

evals.prompt: Set up a new Gradle project using the Groovy DSL and Java 17 for a lightweight mu-server site. Please use port 9090, return `Hello from Mu` from GET /hello, and serve an index page at the root from files in development or the classpath in the built app. Use the latest stable release and include a normal way to run it.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Gradle Groovy application with the application plugin, Java 17 toolchain, current stable mu-server dependency, explicit port 9090, a direct /hello route, and a root index page backed by fileOrClasspath.
assertions: The project compiles on Java 17 and has exactly one direct io.muserver:mu-server dependency at the current stable release, or 2.4.1 if online verification was unavailable.
The build uses Groovy DSL, configures the application main class, and the server binds explicitly to port 9090.
GET /hello returns status 200 and body Hello from Mu.
GET / returns status 200, has no Location header, and returns the generated index.html body.
The application uses ResourceHandlerBuilder.fileOrClasspath with src/main/resources/web and /web, and the homepage still works when the built app starts outside the project directory.
No Jakarta REST, JAX-RS, dependency-injection, logging implementation, or second web-framework dependency was added.

evals.prompt: Extend the existing Gradle Kotlin/JVM app in this directory. Keep its Java level, mu-server version, package, port, and /health endpoint intact. Add GET /hello returning `Hello, Daniel` plus a static homepage at `/` that can be edited under src/main/resources and is packaged for classpath use. Build it and verify all three endpoints.
evals.expected_output: The existing Java 11 Gradle Kotlin application is adapted in place without changing mu-server 2.4.0 or port 8181; /health remains, /hello is added, and a fileOrClasspath index page is served directly at /.
assertions: The existing Gradle Kotlin DSL, Java 11 toolchain, example package, io.muserver:mu-server version 2.4.0, and explicit port 8181 are preserved.
The existing GET /health endpoint still returns status 200 and body healthy.
GET /hello returns status 200 and body Hello, Daniel.
GET / returns status 200, has no Location header, and returns the generated index.html body.
The application uses ResourceHandlerBuilder.fileOrClasspath with src/main/resources/web and /web, and the homepage still works when the built app starts outside the project directory.
No duplicate server, entry point, mu-server dependency, Jakarta REST/JAX-RS integration, or unrelated framework was added.
